board.title: Why Microwaves Heat Soup But Never the Bowl

scenes.narration: Your microwave does not heat food from the outside in. It targets the molecular inside directly.
Deep inside the wall, a magnetron tube fires invisible waves across the chamber at over two billion cycles per second.
scenes.label: 2.45 GHZ

scenes.narration: Every water molecule in your soup is a tiny dipole, with a positive hydrogen side and a negative oxygen side.
As the electric field flips polarity back and forth, the water molecules violently twist to align themselves. This friction creates rapid heat.
Ceramic bowls lack these polar molecules, so the radiation passes right through them while the liquid steams.
The microwave never actually heats your dinner. It forces the water inside to heat itself.
